# Purpose

Demonstrate that an ancestry-confounded synthetic null phenotype can inflate
unadjusted association statistics, then compare it with PC-plus-family/kinship-proxy
adjustment. The workflow is about calibration, not disease modeling.

# Inputs

The bundled runner generates all markers, family labels, ancestry labels, and
phenotypes. A user question about real human data requires a genome build,
cohort manifest, phenotype/covariates, consent-appropriate data access, QC,
and a validated association method; do not substitute this demo.

# Runnable Recipe

```r
system2("Rscript", c(
  "analysis/paper_fig/fig13_human_relatedness_gwas_calibration.R",
  "--out_dir", "analysis/results/human_relatedness_gwas_calibration",
  "--seed", "1301"
))
```

# Interpretation Boundary

The null phenotype has no causal variants. The pass criterion is lower lambda
after adjustment in this fixed synthetic setup, not proof that an adjustment
strategy controls calibration in every human study.
